answer: 340B Savings are used for expanding Patient Services, Improving Access to Care, Strengthening Operations.  At Valley View Health Centers, a division of Community Action Committee of Pike County, we treat all who come to us regardless of their ability to pay. We provide care to patients who live in an area hit hard with the opioid epidemic and poverty. We strive to address social determinants of health by providing access to care, education, housing, transportation, food security, etc. The 340B Drug Discount Program is a federal government program created in 1992 that requires drug manufacturers to provide outpatient drugs to eligible health care organizations and covered entities to stretch scarce federal resources as far as possible, reaching more eligible patients and providing more comprehensive services. We invest in new facilities and equipment to make accessing health care services easier and provide the best in technology and services. We widen our service area through school-based expansion, offer telehealth and remote services to remove geographical barriers. We expand care options by expanding case management services all at locations. We fight food insecurities through a mobile food pantry, increased case management to assist with housing, transportation, etc. We remove barriers by utilize technology to provide access to care using telehealth to reach our most rural patients who may struggle with transportation. We strive to improve insurance verification and authorization process, appointment scheduling and registration, and work to address the shortage of providers. We strive to improve communication, standardized processes, workflows, and leadership that serves to achieve better outcomes for our patients. We work with community partners to build strong relationships that better serve our patients. We strengthen cash on hand to ensure we don’t experience cash shortages that could negatively impact patient access.
